sentences.text: They are heard and perused the case diary.

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code,
1973 for grant of anticipatory bail as he/she is apprehending his/her arrest in connection with Crime No.131/2022 registered at Police Station - Mahila Thana, Neemuch, District -Neemuch (MP) for offence punishable under Section 376 of the IPC.
The allegation against the applicant is of rape of the prosecutrix.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case by the prosecutrix, who happens to be the tenant of the complainant.
Counsel has submitted that even in the date of the incident is said to be 20.12.2006 to 28.2.2022 which has spread over for a period of around 16 years.

sentences.text: Counsel has further submitted that various disputes were going between the parties which is also apparent in the FIR and the complainant made by the prosecutrix.

It is also submitted that a compromise has also been arrived at between the parties in the year 2014 which is also placed on record and there is no such evidence available on record till date which may suggest that the prosecutrix was sexually assaulted by the applicant at any point of time.

Counsel has also drawn attention of this Court to various transactions in which certain amount has been credited in the account of the complainant/prosecutrix and a sum of Rs.3,63,923/-on 13.5.2022; whereas the FIR has been lodged on 16.12.2022 and on 04.09.2018 a sum of Rs.2,17.000/- has also been credited in the account of the complainant and such amount have also been credited in the accounts of the family members of the complainant/prosecutrix.
Thus, it is submitted that the applicant has been black mailed by the complainant/prosecutrix and, hence the applicant deserves to be granted anticipatory bail.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer.

Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case diary including the FIR, this Court finds that various allegations have been levelled against the applicant and the first instance of sexual intercourse is stated to be in the year 2006.

In such circumstances, the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not necessary specially when various transactions have been made between the applicant and the prosecutrix during the course of the years.
Accordingly, the application for anticipatory bail is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant shall be released on bail, upon his/her executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) and furnishing solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
The applicant shall make himself/herself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
The applicant shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
With the aforesaid, this M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per rules.
